correctness.rationale: PASS: For Exp(1), beta=1/2 the true past entropy tends to log4. For every fixed sample of Gaussian kernels, both A_n=int_0^infty f_n and B_n=int_0^infty sqrt(f_n) are finite positive, and estimated entropy converges to L_n=2log B_n-log A_n. On equal-location samples at c, A_n=Phi(c/b_n), B_n=b_n^(1/2)*2^(3/4)*pi^(1/4)*Phi(c/(sqrt2*b_n)), so L_n(c)->log sqrt(8*pi/n) as c->infty, never log4 for any integer n (equality demands n=pi/2). Local dominated convergence yields a positive-probability open neighborhood of samples with nonzero limiting error. On it the nonnegative global squared-error Lebesgue integral diverges, hence its expected value is infinite for EACH n. This is an analytic infinite-tail argument, not a finite simulation. Independently verified Gaussian normalization and exceptional integer n arithmetic.
